claims.text: Nominal 99% confidence intervals produced by modern LLMs cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average on Fermi-style estimation tasks.
Conformal prediction-based interval adjustment achieves accurate 99% observed coverage for LLMs on FermiEval.
Conformal prediction-based adjustment decreases the Winkler interval score of LLM confidence intervals by 54%.
Direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment methods reduce overconfidence in LLMs at high confidence levels.
Under the perception-tunnel theory, LLMs reason under uncertainty by acting as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred probability distribution.
Empirical quantiles of LLM-generated upper and lower bounds form a consistent estimator for the true underlying quantiles under the perception-tunnel model.

evidence.description: Across several modern models, nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
With a conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals, we obtain accurate 99% observed coverage.
And the Winkler interval score decreases by 54%.
For gpt-4o-mini at nominal p=0.95, log-probability observed coverage improves from 0.59 (baseline) to 0.89.
Theory 1 formalizes that the model perceives distribution FI,I+beta where I ~ Unif([0, 1-beta]), neglecting tails.
Theorem 1 proves that (L_hat_n, U_hat_n) converges in probability to (F^-1(alpha/2), F^-1(1 - alpha/2)) independently of perception size beta.

methodologies.name: FermiEval Benchmark
methodologies.description: An evaluation protocol and benchmark of Science Olympiad Fermi estimation questions scored by Winkler interval score for coverage and sharpness.
conditions: Order-of-magnitude integer exponent ground truths between 10^-100 and 10^100

methodologies.name: Split-Conformal Calibration
methodologies.description: A distribution-free post-hoc method that uses a held-out calibration split to calculate nonconformity scores and adjust prediction interval bounds.
conditions: Exchangeability of calibration and test samples

methodologies.name: Direct Log-Probability Elicitation
methodologies.description: Normalizing first-token top-K log probabilities over integer responses into discrete probability distributions to form minimum-mass confidence sets.
conditions: Top-20 log probabilities required from API
Temperature scaling parameter T* fitted on training split

limitations.text: Prior work by Kalyan et al. (2021) focused on reasoning processes in Fermi problem solving rather than evaluating uncertainty quantification via confidence intervals.
Direct log-probability elicitation lacks finite-sample coverage guarantees and exhibits sensitivity to decoding temperature and prompt length.
Log-probability elicitation analysis could only be performed on gpt-4o-mini because other model APIs do not expose sufficient top log probabilities.
Multi-sampling temperature calibration was not evaluated experimentally due to high computational sampling cost.
